title: Draupadi's swayamvara
hook: a bow almost no one can bend, and a mark beyond a device set high in the air
carry: the kings fall, one by one

segments.voice: Yesterday, Draupadi's swayamvara was announced: a princess born from the fire, and five brothers setting out for Panchala.

The arena at Panchala is packed. Kings and princes have come from far and wide, dressed in their best. Brahmins have come to watch. There's music, and the noise of a crowd that has waited for this. Somewhere among the brahmins sit five brothers in borrowed clothes, whom everyone here believes are dead. Then Draupadi enters, carrying a garland, and her brother Dhrishtadyumna rises to announce the terms.
screen: `A PACKED ARENA.` → `FIVE BROTHERS IN DISGUISE.` → `THE TERMS.`

segments.voice: Here's the challenge, in paraphrase. This is the bow, these are the arrows. Up high is a mark, and in front of it a device set in the air, with an opening in it. Whoever strings the bow, shoots through the opening and hits the mark, and is worthy in birth and form and strength, wins my sister. Now a detail the text gives. Drupada had hoped all along to give his daughter to Arjuna, so he had this bow made so stiff that hardly anyone could string it. One by one, the kings try, and the bow beats them. Some can't bend it at all. Some get close, and it springs back and throws them to the ground, their crowns and ornaments scattered across the floor. Great names, humbled in front of everyone. Here's what makes this swayamvara strange. The word means the bride's own choosing. But her choice runs through a test her father set, shaped around one man he hoped would come. The text doesn't say what Draupadi made of it. It shows her standing with the garland while her brother reads out the terms, and the kings walk up to the bow. Some retellings picture the mark as a fish's eye, seen in a reflection. In this passage it's simply a mark, beyond a device, very high up.
screen: `THE TERMS: STRING, SHOOT, HIT.` · `A BOW MADE FOR ONE MAN.` · `THE KINGS FALL, ONE BY ONE.` · `A CHOOSING, ROUTED THROUGH A TEST.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a test you once faced that seemed designed for someone else: a job, a team, a room you didn't quite fit, and notice where the memory sits in the body. With each breath out, let a little of it go. You aren't in that arena now; here, nothing has to be won.
Draupadi's swayamvara. A bow almost no one could bend, a mark beyond a device set high in the air, and kings thrown to the floor.
Your line: the kings fall, one by one. A choosing, routed through a father's test. Day seven hundred forty-one.

howItsDone: The contest at Panchala, with the bow and the mark, is shown in Hindu painting, dance and storytelling; in some retellings the archer aims at a fish's eye seen reflected in water below.

chat.says: If a swayamvara is the bride's choice, why did Draupadi's need a bow contest?
options: Drupada set the test hoping for Arjuna, so her choosing ran through his stiff bow.
Because the kings refused to come unless there was a prize to fight for.
Because Panchala's law said every princess must marry the best archer.
chat.meaning: The text says Drupada hoped to give Draupadi to Arjuna and had the bow made too stiff for others. Her choosing ran through his test.

Arjuna.meaning: the third Pandava brother, a great archer

Dhrishtadyumna.meaning: Draupadi's brother, who announces the terms

swayamvara.meaning: a bride's own choosing of a husband

Panchala.meaning: Drupada's kingdom, where the contest is held

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Swayamvara Parva (the arena; Dhrishtadyumna announces the terms; the bow and the mark; the kings fail)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: the wording of Dhrishtadyumna's terms (including 'birth, form and strength'), the turning device with an opening, and the mark set high.
Confirm that the text says Drupada always hoped to give Draupadi to Arjuna and had the bow made too stiff for others.
Confirm Draupadi enters carrying a garland at this point.
The fish's eye is described only as a detail of 'some retellings'; a Keeper may want to name which.
The three readings of the test were cut in the editor pass (see below).

Editor pass: Ganguli has a 'machine' set up in the sky with an orifice, not clearly a turning one, so 'turning device' became 'a device set in the air' throughout; cut the three-way 'some readers' reading (repeated across nearby days) for a plain observation; 'a favorite scene' made 'shown' (unsourced superlative).
Audit pass: cut 'Arjuna is believed dead. Even so', which put a state of mind in Drupada that the passage doesn't state; the text links the stiff bow to his hope for Arjuna.
